sub_unit_name: Defluoridation- Determination of F ion by ion- selective electrode method

content.title: What is Defluoridation?
content.description: Defluoridation is the process of removing excess fluoride ions (F⁻) from drinking water to make it safe for human consumption.

content.content: Fluoride is naturally present in groundwater due to the dissolution of fluoride-containing minerals. While a small amount of fluoride is beneficial for dental health, excessive fluoride causes dental fluorosis and skeletal fluorosis. Therefore, defluoridation is an essential step in water purification in fluoride-affected regions.

content.title: Safe Fluoride Level
content.content: According to BIS guidelines, the desirable limit of fluoride in drinking water is about 1.0 mg/L, while the maximum permissible limit is 1.5 mg/L.

items.question: Dental Fluorosis
items.answer: Causes discoloration and mottling of teeth.

items.question: Skeletal Fluorosis
items.answer: Leads to joint pain, bone deformities, and stiffness.

items.question: Public Health
items.answer: Provides safe drinking water in fluoride-affected areas.

content.title: Ion-Selective Electrode (ISE)
content.description: An ion-selective electrode is an electrochemical sensor that measures the concentration of a specific ion in a solution by developing a potential proportional to its activity.

content.content: The fluoride ion-selective electrode contains a lanthanum fluoride (LaF₃) crystal membrane. When immersed in a fluoride-containing solution, a potential difference develops across the membrane, which depends on the fluoride ion concentration. This potential is measured using a reference electrode and converted into fluoride concentration.

content.content: The fluoride ion-selective electrode method is widely used in drinking water analysis, groundwater monitoring, environmental laboratories, water treatment plants, and industrial quality control.
